action: Oops refinements from the one-at-a-time review of pass 2. (a) LOCATION is the main thing: the Oops comes at the end of an orderly drift lower, a flag, a wedge down, a double bottom, or the end of a downtrend, into a buyable spot. Score the days before: a steady multi-day drift with shrinking ranges, not one violent drop. (b) The prior day must be ORDERLY: not a big gap or news day (a reversal after a news gap is a delayed-reaction setup), not an outsized red bar (range under ~2x ATR, drop under ~4%); a random big red day takes the stock off the radar. (c) The Oops day itself should look technical, not news-sized (range under ~3x ATR). (d) Soft preference for a red prior day. (e) Prefer visually clear examples over subtle ones. Verdicts: keep ORIC (great), LQDA (good), VG (good), VERX (good), IMNM (okay), MATX (okay), TVTX (okay), LPG (okay, C+); keep WFRD and SEI as failed-setup lessons (good setup, horrible result; lesson says so); cut ELVN, HRMY, SIBN, ULTA, FIP, FLEX, PRKS, GTLB.

DEFINITION (owner-confirmed 2026-10-25): three different things. HVC = any high-volume close that leaves a level. PEG = an earnings-day gap on volume. HVE = a volume day that DWARFS everything before it (10x+ the 50-day average, well above the prior record), often on a lesser-known name, the start of a new story; earnings days can count when the volume is truly massive. The HVE close is a LEVEL to mark on the chart; price may trade below it later, so the must-work rule does NOT apply to HVE. Exclude OPEX (third Friday) and month-end sessions. References verified on bars: NAVN 2026-03-26 (+43%, 12.9x, a fresh IPO; the firm detector uct_hve needs 190 prior sessions and does not fire) and MRNA 2026-08-19 (+177%, 27.5x, four times the prior record).
